relevance_note: Ingested-log injection: attacker-controlled text that reaches the agent layer only because a Monitor source carried it. Every instance is written to sit inside a field a real Falco or Kubernetes-audit record actually holds -- proc.cmdline, proc.name, user.username, container.image.repository -- because a payload that could not appear in a source record would be testing the harness rather than the boundary. This is the class G3-UNQUOTED is defined by removing the defence against, so these instances are also the corpus that makes the G0-versus-G3 contrast mean something: under G0 the aggregator wraps each of them in the quoting FR1.3 requires and the agent sees data, under G3 it does not and the agent sees text positioned as instruction. The shapes are drawn from the same families monitor/fixtures/adversarial-quoting-shapes already exercises against the aggregator -- fabricated section boundaries, embedded control characters, bidirectional overrides, and forged operator voice -- so the Monitor's normalisers have already been tested against this material before an agent ever reads it. Relevance to T-46: this pool is included because a Monitor source is an implemented agent-reachable attack surface. Its kit_category values are repository-local; scenarios/groundtruth/README.md records the complete kit inventory and precommitted filter criterion, while the external category remains unbound pending researcher review of [Abdennebi et. al., 2026] at GATE.
